$comment: Golden runs for the Phase 8 determinism regression. READ validation/golden.ts BEFORE EDITING. This file contains NO simulator output — no AWT, no fingerprint, no passenger count — only the inputs a run is driven from and the NAMES of the keys the persisted envelope carries. That is deliberate: a golden artefact that has to be regenerated whenever elevator behaviour legitimately changes stops being read, and an unread golden is how a real regression ships. Nothing here moves when a dispatcher, a cost term, a weight vector or the physics changes. The only edit this file should ever need is an added or removed key name in an envelopeKeys list, which is a change to the persistence contract and is exactly the change a human should have to look at. If a proposed diff to this file is anything else, it is a bug in the change, not in the manifest.

runs.covers: The cheap two-car hydraulic case, with no sim overrides at all: the minimal envelope, so a new replay knob that is recorded unconditionally shows up here first.

The primary validation building under pure up-peak, with an explicit directional split and two weighted entrances — the demand fields a lighter golden never records. Its seed is above 2^53 on purpose: the decimal-string path is the one a real sweep writes, and Number() would lose it silently.

Access zoning plus a door-obstruction probability, so the run draws from the doors stream as well as the arrivals streams, and four sim knobs are recorded. Its status is timed-out rather than completed, because access-locked-out passengers legitimately keep a run alive to its drain deadline — a stored run that timed out is a real measurement and must replay like any other (reports/replay.ts honours the stored onTimeout for this reason).

A deliberately congested run, and the only golden that reaches the dispatch-retry timer: simulation.ts does not re-offer a call every car refused for a structural reason, so sim.dispatchRetryS is inert everywhere except where a car declines for a soft reason. This run SATURATES, on purpose — a saturated run is a perfectly good determinism fixture and a very bad statistic, and nothing in this suite reads its AWT (CLAUDE.md: flag it, suppress the interval).

Multi-bank with sky-lobby transfers, so transferWalkS and maxEvents are recorded and a journey has more than one leg. Deep tier: it is the slowest of the five and its coverage of the envelope overlaps the always-on set except for those two keys.
The other demand template, the largest building, and the only golden whose window is the constant-ISO measurement slice rather than a rise-and-fall peak. Deep tier on runtime alone.
